fields.title: Segments: which customers are most profitable to sell to
fields.keyTakeaway: Segment customers by margin and cost-to-serve, not by industry vertical. Typically, a small cohort generates most of the profit, while another cohort drains margins through heavy support — yet both look identical on a top-line revenue report.
fields.checkQuestion: A client pays twice the average rate but consumes half of support capacity. How do you determine if they are profitable?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **which segments are most profitable to target?**
fields.blocks/1/subtitle: Categorizes clients by product-market fit alignment
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **A** — the product solves their needs out of the box, willingness to pay is high, support cost is low. Growth is built on them.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **B** — decent fit with minor workarounds, slightly higher cost-to-serve.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **C** — pay reasonably, but demand custom feature tweaks that erode margins.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **D** — small and low-ticket; sustainable only if support cost is near zero.
fields.blocks/1/items/4: **X** — poor fit by definition. Selling to them is destructive: they churn, complain, and consume team bandwidth.
fields.blocks/2/text: **RFM** serves a different purpose — sorting existing clients by recency, frequency, and monetary value. It is an engagement framework for customer retention. **ABC analysis** is simpler: clients (or SKUs) are ranked by revenue contribution, where typically 20% generate roughly 80%.
fields.blocks/3/text:
Margin analysis across 120 clients net of support and custom dev costs:

A — distributors with 15–40 employees, single warehouse, standard workflows: 31 clients, generating 62% of net profit. Support footprint: 20 minutes/month.
C — multi-warehouse chains: 12 clients, paying 3x average ARR, but requesting heavy custom dev; net unprofitable.
X — manufacturing firms: 9 clients, product fails to support their core workflows, average lifespan 5 months, responsible for 1/3 of support tickets.

Action: banned sales to manufacturers, raised prices by 60% for retail chains — four churned, while the remaining eight turned profitable.
fields.blocks/3/title: Kedr: finding who is actually profitable
fields.blocks/4/text: Enterprise logos bring topline ARR and status, while small standardized clients yield actual profit margins. The temptation to build custom product for whales is huge — and often strays companies away from their core profitable niche.
fields.blocks/4/title: The most profitable segment often looks boring
fields.blocks/5/text: Segmentation is a point-in-time snapshot that ages as the product evolves — yesterday's X-tier can become a B-tier. Revisiting it every six months makes sense; doing it more frequently disrupts operational execution.
